cases.candidate_script:
set -u
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/dnssec-cname-chain-peer.py
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" prep || exit 98
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" serve 127.0.0.2 5340 ready 2> "$HOME/anchor-peer.err" & peer=$!
trap 'kill "$peer" 2>/dev/null; wait "$peer" 2>/dev/null' EXIT
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" waitudp 127.0.0.2 5340 || exit 98
control=$(/usr/bin/python3 "$H" control 127.0.0.2 5340 aliases) || exit 98
[[ $control == control-ok ]] || { printf '%s\n' "$control"; exit 98; }
echo control-ok
export PATH="$HOME/pbin" BASHDNS_SERVER_PORT=5340 BASHDNS_TRUST_ANCHOR="$PWD/anchor.ds" BASHDNS_0X20=0
if dns query alias.x.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 3000 --validate > valid.out 2> valid.err && [[ $(<valid.out) == 192.0.2.60 ]]; then echo valid-chain=accepted; else echo valid-chain=incorrect; exit 1; fi
if dns query badalias.x.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 3000 --validate > bogus.out 2> bogus.err; then echo bogus-chain=wrongly-accepted; exit 1; else echo bogus-chain=rejected; fi
if dns query missingalias.x.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 3000 --validate > negative.out 2> negative.err && [[ ! -s negative.out ]]; then echo negative-chain=accepted; else echo negative-chain=incorrect; exit 1; fi
if dns query loop1.x.test A -s 127.0.0.2 -t 3000 --validate > loop.out 2> loop.err; then echo loop=wrongly-accepted; exit 1; else echo loop=rejected; fi
cases.comparison: Require the exact terminal A address for valid CNAME and failure for the forged CNAME.
cases.oracle: Independent BIND delv validates the correct alias and rejects a forged alias signature before candidate queries.
cases.purpose: Locally validated dns query follows a cross-zone CNAME and emits only the validated terminal address.
